reason: Same-type homonyms and stable meaning have coincident type predictions; source inheritance is constructed reader state. No independently observable incompatible requirement is nominated.

design.mechanism: cross-envelope type invariance versus context-conditioned homonymy
design.contrast: Replace the same argument form across two envelope types while holding its local participant relation fixed: its typed role should remain invariant; the homonym model predicts a changed role or incompatible downstream requirement.
design.prediction: GDT559 showed renderer compositionality and inherited successors, but did not test whether a semantic type survives envelope substitution against a homonym rival.
design.countermodel: A renderer or position-conditioned convention can reproduce the observed layouts without the proposed semantic law.
design.falsifier: The held occurrence requires an incompatible role or the invariant type fits only by changing the surrounding construction.
design.principal_risk: The four argument types and independent participant endpoints are unresolved; use only abstract type constraints.
design.smallest_test: Select one form occurring in two envelopes, hold one occurrence out, and compare role compatibility under invariant-type and homonym models.
design.prior_duplicate_pointers: Near GDT559 and IDEA000064/078; distinct observable is type preservation across envelope substitution.
design.selection_status: raw unreviewed; no readiness or novelty claim

blockers.detail: Context-dependent meanings need not change semantic type; role change need not change lexical meaning.
GDT559 reader defaults and GDT593 applications do not supply an independent type endpoint.

all_of.detail: Specify finite source-bound rival predictions for an observable relation or requirement; joint inference without pretranslated words is allowed.
Bind that observable independently of renderer-assigned meaning or inherited context state.

not_sufficient: More unchanged formal envelopes, renderer inheritance matches, or invariant abstract types alone.
